Part 1: LESSON OBJECTIVE
Find cone volume, curved and total surface area, slant height, and missing dimensions.
Part 2: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
A cone has a circular base and a vertex. Its volume is one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and perpendicular height.
Part 3: KEY DEFINITIONS
Radius r is half the base diameter; h is perpendicular height; slant height l is the straight distance along the side from rim to vertex.
Part 4: CORE RULE
V=πr²h/3; curved surface area=πrl; total surface area=πr(l+r). For a right cone, l²=r²+h².
Part 5: HOW IT WORKS
Choose volume or surface area; identify r, h, l; convert units; substitute; use π exactly unless decimals are requested.
Part 6: WORKED EXAMPLE 1
A cone radius 3 cm and height 4 cm has volume π×9×4/3=12π cm³, exactly one-third of its matching cylinder.
Part 7: WORKED EXAMPLE 2
A cone radius 2 m and height 9 m has volume π×4×9/3=12π m³.
Part 8: WORKED EXAMPLE 3
For volume 48π cm³ and radius 4 cm, 48=16h/3; multiplying by three gives h=9 cm.
Part 9: WORKED EXAMPLE 4
For volume 75π cm³ and height 9 cm, 75=3r², so r²=25 and positive r=5 cm.
Part 10: WORKED EXAMPLE 5
For a right cone r=6 and h=8, l=√(36+64)=10. Curved area=60π and total area=96π cm².
Part 11: VERIFIED RIGHT-CONE DIAGRAM
A deterministic diagram uses r=6, h=8 and slant=10, a verified Pythagorean triple.
Part 12: VOLUME COMPARISON
A cone and cylinder with the same radius and height have volumes in the ratio 1:3; the cone is one-third.
Part 13: DIAMETER AND UNITS
If diameter=10 cm, radius=5 cm. Convert all measurements before applying any formula; volume units are cubed.
Part 14: SIMILARITY
When all lengths scale by k, surface area scales by k² and volume by k³. Doubling dimensions multiplies volume by eight.
Part 15: COMMON MISTAKES
Do not confuse radius with diameter, height with slant height, curved area with total area, or forget the one-third factor.
Part 16: EXAM STRATEGY AND QUICK CHECK
Identify the requested quantity before selecting the formula. Quick check: r=2, h=6 gives V=8π; r=3, l=5 gives total area=24π.
Part 17: LESSON RECAP AND NEXT STEP
Use V=πr²h/3, curved=πrl, total=πr(l+r), and l²=r²+h². Complete 18 practice questions and the five-question test.
